The human plateau shattered. The posts spread like wildfire across social media feeds—it was primetime, just before the end of the workday. The viewer count instantly jumped from two hundred thousand to two hundred and fifty thousand. Online media bots latched onto the event and began churning out stories about the provocative stream by "the most innovative business coach of our generation." A woman, no less!

Now, three hundred and fifty thousand people from around the globe were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freya a question. Three hundred and sixty. Three hundred and seventy. Every new thousand took Freya's breath away. And then it was time to answer.

The main thing was not to let this chat with her followers devolve into a group Tinder date.

*"Do you have kids?"* a stranger asked. *"How do you succeed when you have four of them?"*

Freya was tempted to answer, *"You don't."* However, for one thing, stay-at-home moms made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so it was a sore subject. For another, you couldn't say that to a follower who had most likely scraped together those fifty bucks from her kids' lunch money. Instead, Freya fell back on a polite, well-rehearsed answer.

"Everyone defines success for themselves," she said. "If your dream has always been to be a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to your investment strategy and never hand your capital over to unvetted funds."

*"Are you married?"* someone asked, donating the five-dollar minimum.

Freya now simply ignored questions like that. Thankfully, a flood of more interesting (and higher-paying!) questions flushed all the cheap bait straight down the drain.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was loving it, and the viewer count kept climbing—a clip of her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. With fame, though, comes responsibility: the questions took a sharp turn straight into group-Tinder-date territory.
